mood: Landscape painting of two unequal iris foliage islands across a broad blue-lilac interval. A dominant hooked forest-green blade arches partway across the gap; smaller spears and crossing leaves stop short. Sparse crumpled yellow-ochre and violet-pink blossoms droop on thin stems. Broken cream and lavender curls weave around both clusters, pale loops threading the lower-right leaves. Bristle-drag paint, diffuse light.
material_language: Directional teal and forest-green leaf strokes with bristle drag and broken pigment coverage
Opaque cream, lilac and blue-gray scumbles interrupted by dark green underlayers
Small irregular yellow-ochre and violet-pink petal daubs on thin painted stems
lighting: Diffuse painted light throughout; pale broken strokes surround dark leaf silhouettes without crisp cast shadows or sculptural cutaway depth.
object_inventory: A long hooked forest-green iris blade with a broken teal brushstroke edge.
negative_constraints: No abstract fold, cutaway, punched hole or unrelated pigment macro; retain recognizable iris leaves, thin stems and irregular blossoms.
No reconstruction of the original thicket, blossom count or placement; do not erase the blue-lilac separation.
No text, labels, logos, interface chrome, target rings, pins, debug marks, pasted cards or framed source panels.
No stretching, forced cropping or padding; reference dimensions do not dictate the output canvas.
No horizon, room, city, metaphor scene, crisp cast shadows or clean outlined petals.
Only the dominant hooked blade is the owning source mark; subordinate foliage and blossoms are not additional source windows.
